chunks: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

Al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام said: “Whoever does not have an admonisher from his heart, a restrainer from his self, and does not have a guiding companion, his enemy gains mastery over his neck.”

key_terms.زَاجِرٌ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: an internal restraint that checks the self
key_terms.عَدُوُّهُ: his enemy, meaning the force that overcomes and misleads him
key_terms.قَرِينٌ مُرْشِدٌ: a companion who provides sound guidance
key_terms.مِنْ عُنُقِهِ: over his neck, an expression for gaining control over him
key_terms.وَاعِظٌ مِنْ قَلْبِهِ: an inner admonisher arising from the heart

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe the role of inner conscience and righteous companionship in protecting a person?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a person needs inner moral awareness, self-restraint, and righteous guidance in order to remain protected. Without these supports, one's enemy is able to overpower him, pointing to the spiritual danger of heedlessness and the importance of disciplined companionship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5866 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said that Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), peace be upon him, said:
"Whoever does not have an inner advisor from his heart, a restrainer from his own soul, and a guiding companion, his enemy will easily gain control over him."
